q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Some plant diseases are indeed difficult to ______ because they can spread rapidly and easily, impacting multiple plants in a vast area.
exp: 빠르고 쉽게 퍼져 넓은 지역의 식물에 영향을 준다는 이유가 이어지므로, 그런 병은 "뿌리 뽑기"(eradicate) 어렵다는 말이 알맞다. nourish(영양분을 주다)와 proliferate(급증하다)는 병을 없앤다는 문맥과 맞지 않고, 널리 퍼지는 병은 오히려 눈에 띄므로 detect(발견하다)도 이유와 어울리지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

In the business world, ______ is highly valued as it showcases a person’s commitment to meeting deadlines and respecting others’ time.
exp: 마감을 지키고 다른 사람의 시간을 존중하는 태도를 보여 주는 것은 punctuality(시간 엄수)이다. humility(겸손), sincerity(성실·진실함), frugality(검소)는 시간과 직접 관련이 없다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Preliminary investigations indicate that some, if not all, of the clients’ money, ______ to be $6 million in total, has found its way into unquoted companies and property purchases.
exp: that절의 동사는 has found이므로 쉼표 사이의 빈칸은 the clients’ money를 꾸미는 삽입구이다. 돈은 총 600만 달러로 "여겨지는" 대상이므로 (which is) believed to be의 과거분사 believed가 알맞다. believe와 believes는 동사가 겹치고, believing은 능동이라 뜻이 맞지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Yuna (10:30 am): Hi Jenny, I need your advice on buying a car.
Jenny (10:31 am): Hi, do you want to buy a car? What kind of car?
Yuna (10:32 am): Maybe a mid-sized sedan or an SUV.
Jenny (10:32 am): An SUV is more practical.
Yuna (10:33 am): SUVs are more expensive than sedans. ______.
Jenny (10:34 am): One of my friends is a used car dealer. He can give you a good deal.
Yuna (10:34 am): Really? That would be nice.
Jenny (10:35 am): Do you want his number?
Yuna (10:35 am): Sure.
Jenny (10:35 am): Just one second.
Jenny (10:36 am): 707-123-5678
Yuna (10:36 am): Thanks!
opts: I need to get in shape
I can pick you up later
exp: SUV가 세단보다 비싸다는 말에 이어지고, Jenny가 싸게 해 줄 수 있는 중고차 딜러 친구를 소개하므로 "예산이 빠듯하다"(I’m on a tight budget)가 알맞다. 몸매 관리, 날씨가 곧 갤 것이라는 말, 나중에 태우러 가겠다는 말은 차 값 이야기와 이어지지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

A: How many copies of the presentation materials do you think we’ll need?
B: 60 should be enough, but it’s always good to have extras.
A: True. Better safe than sorry. How many would you recommend then?
B: Let’s make it 75 just in case we have more attendees than expected like last time.
A: Good idea. ______?
B: Absolutely. We are going to have people asking for the presentation materials after the presentation.
A: Sure, that way everyone can easily have it whenever needed.
opts: How early do we need to distribute the materials
Should we also have a digital version for sharing
Will the materials be printed in color or black and white
Are there any specific materials we should avoid including
exp: B가 "물론이죠. 발표가 끝난 뒤 자료를 달라는 사람들이 있을 거예요"라고 답하고 A가 "그러면 누구나 필요할 때 쉽게 가질 수 있겠다"고 하므로, 빈칸은 공유용 디지털 자료도 준비할지를 묻는 말이다. 나머지는 Absolutely로 답할 수 없거나(시기, 컬러 여부) 뒤 내용과 이어지지 않는다.

q:
(A)에 들어갈 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

(A) ______

We have been notified of a scam targeting people through text messages requesting they pay an overdue parking ticket.
• These text messages are not from us.
• Do not click the link or provide payment details.
• Report these messages to your cell phone provider and then delete them.
• We do not notify the public of fines through texting, media, or social media.

City-approved notification methods for parking tickets:
• Ticket served to vehicle
• Ticket sent by post to registered owner of vehicle
opts: How to Avoid Getting Parking Tickets
Save Time and Money! Helpful Parking Tips
Alert! Fake Parking Ticket Payment Text Messages
exp: 밀린 주차 위반 과태료를 내라는 문자 사기가 있으니 링크를 누르지 말고 신고한 뒤 지우라고 알리는 글이므로 "주의! 가짜 주차 위반 과태료 납부 문자"가 제목으로 알맞다. 납부 방법, 주차 위반을 피하는 법, 주차 요령을 설명하는 글이 아니다.

q:
윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

(A) ______

We have been notified of a scam targeting people through text messages requesting they pay an overdue parking ticket.
• These text messages are not from us.
• Do not click the link or provide payment details.

City-approved notification methods for parking tickets:

opts: 전달된 링크에 결제 세부 정보를 입력해야 한다.
고지서는 등록된 차량 소유주에게 우편으로 발송된다.
exp: 시가 승인한 통지 방법으로 "Ticket sent by post to registered owner of vehicle"이 있으므로 등록된 차량 소유주에게 우편으로 보낸다는 말이 일치한다. 링크를 누르거나 결제 정보를 주지 말라고 했고, 문자는 신고한 뒤 삭제하라고 했으며, 시는 문자로 벌금을 알리지 않는다고 했으므로 나머지는 틀리다.

q:
밑줄 친 critical의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

Health for People (https://healthforpeople.or.kr)

Health for People

People should be able to live a happy, healthy, and prosperous life. Health is a substantial part of human right, and makes a __critical__ contribution to societal well-being, economic growth, and peace.

But access to health is not equitable.

The National Health Center Foundation (NHC Foundation) is here to support the National Health Center (NHC) to achieve its vision of a nation in which all people attain the highest level of health. The NHC aims to promote health and serve the vulnerable. The NHC Foundation is committed to helping the NHC by partnering with diverse actors, including businesses, philanthropists, and the general public.
exp: 건강이 사회의 안녕, 경제 성장, 평화에 "매우 중요한" 기여를 한다는 문맥이므로 critical은 pivotal(중추적인, 아주 중요한)과 뜻이 가깝다. perilous(위험한), analytical(분석적인), judgmental(비판적인)은 critical의 다른 뜻이거나 관계없는 뜻이다.

윗글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

opts: 의료비 지원이 필요한 사람들을 위한 기부를 독려하려고
행복하고 건강한 삶을 위한 캠페인을 제안하려고

q:
다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

To: chlsbrown@cbsys.com
From: tomsmith@boogle.com
Date: June 21, 2025

I am writing to thank you for the interview last week. I truly enjoyed our conversation. The information you shared about your new Account Management System was very valuable.

opts: to set up an interview appointment
to inquire about updates on the decision process
to request more information about the company’s business

q:
다음 글에서 The National Independence Museum에 대한 내용과 일치하는 것은?

NIM (https://nim.memorial.or.kr)

The National Independence Museum

The National Independence Museum preserves the national history through exhibitions, research, and educational programs, while fostering national pride. We invite you to experience this legacy and hear the enduring calls for peace in a scenic rural setting.

Major Projects
－ Exhibitions & Collection Management: A total of 150,000 relics of the independence movement are displayed in eight exhibition halls.
－ Research: Dedicated to the study of the independence movement, the Museum supports scholarly work on related historical topics.
－ Education: Through educational programs, the Museum promotes the national identity and deepens historical understanding among citizens.
－ Cultural Events: Regular cultural events are held to provide visitors with insights into the national history and culture.
opts: It is located in an urban environment surrounded by many skyscrapers.
It displays more than a million artifacts related to the independence movement.
It supports educational activities instead of scholarly projects.
It offers visitors cultural events on a regular basis.
exp: "Regular cultural events are held"라고 했으므로 정기적으로 문화 행사를 연다는 말이 일치한다. 박물관은 경치 좋은 시골(a scenic rural setting)에 있고, 전시 유물은 15만 점이며, 교육뿐 아니라 학술 연구(scholarly work)도 지원하므로 나머지는 틀리다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.

We tend (1) __to imagine__ Robin Hood and outlaws in general as fugitives because they defied the king’s officials and operated (2) __outside the law__ in the great forests of the kingdom. What we forget is that there (3) __were__ an established process behind the creation of outlaws. On the whole, men did not choose to become outlaws; they (4) __were made__ outlaws.
exp: there 구문의 동사는 뒤에 오는 주어에 수를 맞추는데, 주어가 단수인 an established process이므로 were가 아니라 was여야 한다. tend to imagine은 tend가 to부정사를 취한 것, outside the law는 "법 밖에서"라는 전치사구, were made outlaws는 "make + 목적어 + 보어"의 수동태로 모두 옳다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.

The olive tree was (1) __such a driving force__ in the economies of the Ancient Greek city-states (2) __that__ it was believed (3) __to have been__ a gift of gods―namely from Athena, the goddess of wisdom, (4) __whom__ Athens took its name.
exp: "Athens took its name from Athena"에서 온 관계절이므로 전치사 from이 필요해 from whom이어야 한다. whom만 쓰면 뒤가 완전한 절이라 맞지 않는다. "such a + 명사 ... that"은 "매우 ~해서 …하다"의 구문이고, to have been은 믿어진 시점보다 앞선 일을 나타내는 완료부정사로 모두 옳다.

q:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

The reason artificial blue light in devices can be so harmful in the evening is that it mimics the sun’s natural blue light―which confuses the body’s circadian clock. A study showed that viewing artificial blue light in the evening will push sleep-inducing melatonin hormones down drastically, disrupting bedtimes and affecting daytime behavior. But getting that same blue light from the sun, which contains a health-boosting full spectrum of light, does the opposite. According to the study, the more daytime blue light a person gets, the better defense they have against the harms of evening blue light from screens. Thus, packing the day with sunshine creates a blue-light build-up that helps counteract the consequences of that artificial light at night. In other words, the more sunlight exposure a child gets during the day, the better their brain can build a wall against the harms of artificial blue light later.
opts: Sunlight’s help in fighting artificial blue light effects
The dangers of using devices during the day
How screens affect children’s sleep cycles
Why melatonin levels drop in the evening
exp: 낮에 햇빛을 많이 쬘수록 저녁에 화면에서 나오는 인공 블루라이트의 해로움을 더 잘 막는다는 것이 글의 결론이므로 "인공 블루라이트의 영향에 맞서는 데 햇빛이 주는 도움"이 주제이다. 낮의 기기 사용 위험은 언급되지 않고, 화면이 수면에 미치는 영향과 멜라토닌 감소는 도입부의 일부 내용일 뿐이다.

q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Usually toddlers picking things up from the ground means trouble.

(A) The family reported the find to the Israel Antiquities Authority, which determined it is a beetle-shaped seal from the Middle Bronze Age.
(B) But as 3-year-old Ziv Nitzan of Israel brushed away the sand on what seemed to be a rock, she revealed a nearly 4,000-year-old Egyptian artifact.
(C) Ziv was awarded a certificate for good citizenship, and the Heritage Minister of Israel said the seal “connects us to a grand story,” and that “even children can be a part of discovering history.”
exp: "아기가 땅에서 뭔가 줍는 것은 보통 골칫거리"라는 말 뒤에 But으로 시작해 Ziv가 유물을 발견한 일을 소개하는 (B)가 온다. 그 발견물(the find)을 가족이 신고해 인장으로 판정받는 (A)가 이어지고, 그 결과 Ziv가 표창을 받고 장관이 the seal을 언급하는 (C)가 마지막이다.

q:
주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은?

However, according to Mike Tipton, a professor at University of Portsmouth, this is far from the quickest way of lowering your body temperature.

There are plenty of simple, scientifically supported techniques that will help you handle the heat. (1) If you’re feeling the heat and somebody offers you a fan, it’s likely that you’ll try and cool your face first. (2) Certainly, all that breeze on your face will stimulate cold receptors there, which will give you a very powerful sensation of comfort. But actually, it’s not going to extract the heat from your body. Instead, a better cooling strategy is to immerse your hands in cold water for 15 to 20 minutes. (3) Your hands have a high surface area to mass area―they have lots of blood flowing in them when you’re hot. (4) If your core temperature is hot, your body will send blood to the extremities in order to lose heat.
exp: 주어진 문장의 this는 "부채로 얼굴부터 식히는 것"을 가리키므로 그 내용 바로 뒤인 (2)에 들어가야 한다. 그러면 "그것은 체온을 가장 빨리 낮추는 방법이 아니다 → 물론(Certainly) 얼굴의 바람은 시원한 느낌을 주지만 → 실제로는 몸의 열을 빼내지 못한다"로 자연스럽게 이어진다.

q:
다음 글의 흐름상 어색한 문장은?

Scientists in the UK grew special tomatoes with extra vitamin D, which is important for people’s health. Vitamin D deficiency affects about one billion people worldwide. (1) __Tomatoes naturally contain a substance that gets converted into vitamin D.__ (2) __The team altered the genes of the tomato plants, breeding them to have more of this substance than usual.__ (3) __Each tomato came to have about as much vitamin D as two medium-sized eggs.__ (4) __Moreover, tomatoes are commonly eaten raw in salads and served as a cooked vegetable.__ The scientists think the technique could be used with other foods, too.
exp: 글은 유전자를 바꿔 비타민 D가 많은 토마토를 만든 연구(원래 들어 있는 물질 → 유전자 변형 → 결과 → 다른 식품에도 적용 가능)를 차례로 설명한다. (4)는 토마토를 먹는 방법에 대한 말이어서 연구 이야기의 흐름과 관계가 없다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

A hunter-gatherer in the Stone Age knew how to make her own clothes, how to start a fire, how to hunt rabbits and how to escape lions. We think we know far more today, but as individuals, we actually know far less. We rely on the expertise of others for almost all our needs. In one humbling experiment, people were asked to evaluate how well they understood the workings of an ordinary zipper. Most people confidently replied that they understood zippers very well―after all, they use them all the time. They were then asked to describe in as much detail as possible all the steps involved in the zipper’s operation. Most people had no idea. This is what Steven Sloman and Philip Fernbach have termed ‘the knowledge illusion’. We think we know a lot, even though individually we know very little, because we treat knowledge ______ as if it were our own.
exp: 우리는 거의 모든 일에서 남의 전문 지식에 기대면서도 스스로 많이 안다고 착각한다는 내용이므로, "다른 사람의 머릿속에 있는" 지식을 내 것처럼 여긴다는 말이 알맞다. 직접 겪은 경험, 교육, 시행착오로 얻은 지식은 실제로 자기 지식이어서 "착각"이라는 요지와 맞지 않는다.

q:
밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

A gazelle on the African savanna is trying not to be eaten by cheetahs, but it is also trying to outrun other gazelles when a cheetah attacks. What matters to the gazelle is being faster than other gazelles, not being faster than cheetahs. In the same way, psychologists sometimes wonder why people are endowed with the ability to learn the part of Hamlet or understand calculus when neither skill was of much use to mankind in the primitive conditions where his intellect was shaped. Einstein would probably have been as hopeless as anybody in working out how to catch a woolly rhinoceros. Nicholas Humphrey, a Cambridge psychologist, was the first to see clearly the solution to this puzzle. We use our intellects not to solve practical problems but to outwit each other. Deceiving people, detecting deceit, understanding people’s motives, manipulating people―these are what intellect is used for. So what matters is ______.
opts: not how clever and crafty you are but how much more clever and craftier you are than other people
that individuals act according to their collective interest rather than their own personal interest
to design a society where members cooperate to find optimal solutions to benefit themselves
coming up with the best solution to practical problems in a given condition
exp: 가젤에게 중요한 것이 치타보다 빠른 것이 아니라 다른 가젤보다 빠른 것이듯, 지능도 실용적 문제 해결이 아니라 서로를 앞지르는 데 쓰인다고 했다. 따라서 중요한 것은 얼마나 영리한가가 아니라 남보다 얼마나 더 영리한가이다. 집단의 이익, 협력하는 사회, 실용적 문제의 해결은 글의 주장과 반대된다.
